# Christopher Heskett

Canonical URL: https://chrisaheskett.vercel.app/
Experience: https://chrisaheskett.vercel.app/record
Structured JSON: https://chrisaheskett.vercel.app/portfolio.json

## Summary

Current work includes a full-size pinball machine, an AI-vision robotics arm, a self-watering planter PCB, and a subpixel image editor.

## Main Projects

### Garden Party Pinball
Status: In progress
Context: Solo build
Label: pinball machine
I'm building a full-size homebrew pinball machine around FAST control hardware and Mission Pinball Framework. I designed and assembled the cabinet, playfield mechanisms, control board, wiring, and game logic. The machine currently powers up with the playfield installed while I rework the cabinet fit and final geometry.
Published media: 2

### VividGrasp AI-Vision Robotics Arm
Status: Completed team project
Context: Team of 10, Stanford AI4ALL
Label: robotics simulation
Source: https://github.com/LenekyRadish/VividGrasp
Best link label: Open source
My contribution: I led CAD, modeled the arm in SolidWorks, prepared its URDF files, and worked with a teammate on a physical prototype.
Related program/logo link: https://ai4all.spcs.stanford.edu/
A ten-person Stanford AI4ALL project combining computer vision, inverse kinematics, and PyBullet simulation to move a robotic arm toward recognized objects.
Published media: 4

### Smart Self-Watering Pot / Smart Planter PCB
Status: Prototype in progress
Context: Solo prototype
Label: plant-watering prototype
Related program/logo link: https://tetc.org/
Related program context: Well... kinda. Coach Taylor, my ninth grade coach at the TETC challenged me to make this, so while it wasn't a lesson, it has a connection to TETC.
I designed and assembled an ESP32-based controller for a self-watering planter. The fabricated PCB reads soil moisture, controls a water pump, and integrates display and physical input hardware. I also designed the planter, reservoir, and electronics layout in SolidWorks.
Published media: 4; interactive 3D models: 1

### Subpix
Context: Solo software project
Label: desktop app
Project: https://subpix-editor.vercel.app/
Source: https://github.com/Chrissyuh/Subpix
Best link label: Open app
I built Subpix, an open-source desktop editor for drawing with individual RGB subpixels. It reads and validates .subpix JSON files, exports PNG images, and ships as a packaged Windows application built with Electron, React, TypeScript, and Vite.
Published media: 2

## More Work

- AgentDeck - standard - local-network controller: I built AgentDeck to turn an old phone or tablet into a dedicated touchscreen controller for AI coding agents. A lightweight desktop host serves the interface over the local network, allowing spare hardware to replace an expensive single-purpose control deck. ([source](https://github.com/Chrissyuh/agentdeck)). Published media: 1.
- Check-ins - standard - React / Vite web app: I built Check-ins, a local-first web app for recurring work and study tasks. It tracks target and maximum gaps, flags items that are due or overdue, and keeps a completion history without requiring an account. ([project](https://check-ins-zeta.vercel.app/), [source](https://github.com/Chrissyuh/check-ins)). Published media: 1.
- VEX Robotics Builds - standard - TETC robotics builds: I built VEX robots at TETC to practice gearing, drivetrain layout, shaft spacing, and mechanical packaging. Published media: 0.
- MIDI Practice Tool - compact - Python / music: A small Python tool for keyboard practice, soundfonts, pedals, and control mapping. Published media: 0.
- Desmos 3D Solar System - compact - math visualization: An interactive 3D orbit scene built in Desmos to experiment with surfaces, motion, and performance limits. ([project](https://www.desmos.com/3d/qcjp33t4ij)). Published media: 0.
- TinyGPT Experiments - compact - machine learning: Small next-token-model experiments used to study training behavior and instruction behavior. Published media: 0.
